case_name: M/S Ayodhya Faizabad Developement vs Dy. Commissioner Of Income Tax

parties.respondent_defendant: DCIT (Exemption), Lines, Faizabad (formerly Ayodhya Circle- Lucknow Faizabad Development Authority) (Respondent)

facts_of_case: Assessee authority filed appeals against various orders passed by the ld. CIT(A) at Lucknow and NFAC.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the assessee to substantiate its claim that it is a charitable trust.
legal_principles.held: It was unable to respond to the query as to how the sales of properties made by it had benefited the weaker sections. It was also unable to demonstrate that the properties were disposed of on cost-to-cost basis, as the assessee had not submitted any details in this regard.

legal_principles.principle: A commercial enterprise cannot be disguised as a charitable trust by charging interest on delayed payments.
legal_principles.held: The assessee charged its customers for each and every facility that it provided and was therefore, operating on the lines of a commercial enterprise.

legal_principles.principle: The law is clear that a charitable trust must demonstrate its charitable purpose and not just claim it.
legal_principles.held: It had more than Rs.11.11 Crores of investment in the form of FDRs and savings accounts and was earning interest on the same. This earning of interest was devoid of any charitable purpose and was also not incidental to the nature of activity performed by the assessee.

outcome.final_order: The assessee's appeals were partly allowed for the assessment years 2017-18 and 2018-19.
